statements: Create pairing.mjs at the workspace root: an ES module with one named function export, pairRound(players, history). Use Node.js built-ins only and no dependencies. Tests, if you write any, go under test/.

players and history must each be an array, otherwise throw a TypeError whose code property is 'E_TYPE'. Each player must be a non-null, non-array object with a non-empty string id and safe-integer points and rating, and ids must be distinct, otherwise throw a RangeError with code 'E_PLAYER'. Extra fields are ignored.

Each history entry must be an array [idA, idB] where idA is the id of a player in this call and idB is either null (idA had a bye) or the id of a different player in this call (the two have met; their order in the entry does not matter and an entry may repeat). Otherwise throw a RangeError with code 'E_HISTORY'. The checks run in the order E_TYPE, E_PLAYER, E_HISTORY, before any pairing.

Players are ranked best first: more points first, then higher rating first, then id ascending compared as plain strings by UTF-16 code unit order (so "10" ranks before "9" and "B" before "a"). Ranks are always distinct because ids are.

Two players who have met must not be paired. With an odd number of players exactly one gets a bye and all the others are paired; with an even number nobody gets a bye. A player who has had a bye in history must not get another. The bye goes to the lowest ranked player among those who may take it with all the others then still pairable.

The others are paired as the lexicographically first valid set, walking the ranked list: the highest ranked unpaired player takes the highest ranked still unpaired player they have not met for whom all remaining unpaired players can still be paired validly; then repeat. The bye player is chosen first and left out of this walk.

The result is an array of [idA, idB] pairs with the higher ranked player first, ordered by the rank of idA, best first. A bye, if any, is the last element, written [id, null]. With no players the result is []. The result is a new array and the arguments are not mutated.
If no valid complete pairing exists, including an odd number of players where nobody may take the bye, throw a RangeError with code 'E_NO_PAIRING'.
brief: Implement pairing.mjs exactly as the numbered statements specify, then stop. Do not change any other file except tests under test/.
